ai.description: *Hemiphyllodactylus jnana* is a small gecko reaching 35–40 mm SVL. It is pale brown with dark dorsal blotches and a distinct white tail tip. It lacks enlarged subdigital lamellae on the first toe.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemiphyllodactylus jnana* is distinguished from other Indian congeners by the presence of a distinct, dark-edged pale spot on the nape, rather than a continuous dorsal stripe.
ai.habitat: *Hemiphyllodactylus jnana* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, typically inhabiting moist deciduous forests at elevations ranging from 800 to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemiphyllodactylus jnana* is a nocturnal gecko that actively hunts small invertebrates on rock surfaces and tree trunks under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemiphyllodactylus jnana* is oviparous, typically laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemiphyllodactylus jnana* is endemic to the high-elevation shola forests of the Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically found above 1,500 meters.
